items.title: Cabazitaxel, Carboplatin, Cetrelimab, and Niraparib for Aggressive Variant Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial tests a combination approach for aggressive variant metastatic prostate cancer. Patients receive chemotherapy (cabazitaxel and carboplatin) plus immunotherapy (cetrelimab), followed by a PARP inhibitor (niraparib) with or without continued immunotherapy. The study is no longer recruiting new patients but is still active.

items.title: AZD0516 Monotherapy and Combination for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This early-stage Phase 1/2 trial is testing the safety and tolerability of AZD0516, a new investigational drug, alone and in combination with other anti-cancer agents. The trial is currently recruiting patients with metastatic prostate cancer to determine appropriate dosing and identify potential treatment combinations.

items.title: Talazoparib Plus Enzalutamide Before Surgery for Lymph Node Positive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial studies adding talazoparib (a PARP inhibitor) to standard hormone therapy and enzalutamide before surgery in patients with prostate cancer that has spread to lymph nodes. The goal is to determine if this combination is more effective than standard treatment alone in this pre-surgical setting.

items.title: Risk-Adapted Treatment with De-escalation for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 study tests whether treatment can be safely reduced over time in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients after initial intensive therapy. The goal is to maintain cancer control while reducing side effects and improving quality of life through personalized treatment adjustment based on individual response.

items.title: HER2-Targeted Immune Cells for Metastatic Breast and Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial uses specially modified immune cells (armed with antibodies targeting HER2) to treat metastatic breast or prostate cancer. Patients receive weekly infusions followed by bi-weekly treatments. The study evaluates safety and early signs of effectiveness of this immune cell therapy approach.

items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone vs Standard Care in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares xaluritamig (a novel bispecific antibody) combined with abiraterone against standard chemotherapy or hormone therapy in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have not yet received chemotherapy. The primary goal is to determine if the combination improves overall survival.

items.title: Safety Study of Xaluritamig in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial evaluates the safety profile of xaluritamig, a bispecific antibody, in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and aims to establish the appropriate dose and identify side effects before larger trials.

items.title: Carboplatin for Metastatic Prostate Cancer with DNA Repair Gene Alterations
items.summary: This completed Phase 2 study evaluated carboplatin chemotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients with mutations in DNA repair genes (homologous recombination pathway). The trial aimed to determine if these genetic alterations predict response to platinum-based chemotherapy.

items.title: Radium-223 With or Without M3814 and Avelumab for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial compares radium-223 (a radioactive treatment for bone metastases) alone, with M3814 (a DNA repair inhibitor), or with both M3814 and avelumab (immunotherapy). The study seeks to determine the optimal combination to improve treatment of bone metastases in castration-resistant prostate cancer.

items.title: Tinengotinib Combined with Standard Treatments for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial tests the safety of tinengotinib, a new investigational drug, when combined with standard hormone therapies (abiraterone or enzalutamide) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting patients to determine if this combination causes acceptable side effects.

items.title: BL-B01D1 Combination Therapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2/3 study will test BL-B01D1 combination therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial will first conduct a Phase 2 study to evaluate preliminary effectiveness and safety before potentially advancing to a larger Phase 3 trial.

items.title: Combination Alpha and Lutetium PSMA Radioligand Therapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial combines two types of radioactive treatments targeting PSMA on prostate cancer cells: actinium-225 (alpha radiation) and lutetium-177 (beta radiation). The study aims to find the safest dose of this dual radioligand approach for progressive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

items.title: Dual-Target PSMA/PSCA CAR-NK Cell Therapy for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial tests a novel cell therapy using engineered natural killer (NK) cells that target two proteins on prostate cancer cells: PSMA and PSCA. The study evaluates safety and early effectiveness of this dual-targeting approach in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

items.title: Olaparib Plus Radium-223 for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer with Bone Metastases
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial studies the combination of olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) with radium-223 (radioactive treatment) in castration-resistant prostate cancer patients with bone metastases. The study, no longer recruiting, aims to find the best dose and evaluate effectiveness of combining DNA repair inhibition with targeted radiation.

items.title: Lead-212 Radioligand Therapy Targeting GRPR in Advanced Cancers
items.summary: This first-in-human Phase 1 trial tests a radioactive drug (lead-212) that targets the gastrin-releasing peptide receptor (GRPR) found on some cancer cells. The study evaluates safety, radiation dosing, and early effectiveness in patients with advanced cancers expressing GRPR, including prostate cancer.

items.title: GDC-1261 for Advanced or Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial evaluates GDC-1261, a new investigational drug, in advanced or metastatic prostate cancer. The study is recruiting patients to assess safety, how the drug is processed by the body, and early signs of anti-tumor activity to determine recommended doses for future studies.

items.title: Multi-Target Radioligand Therapy for Metastatic Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial evaluates personalized radioligand therapy targeting PSMA, SSTR2, or GRPR based on which target is most expressed in metastatic neuroendocrine prostate cancer. The study tracks how tumor target expression changes with treatment and is no longer recruiting.

items.title: Pocenbrodib Alone or With Darolutamide for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial tests pocenbrodib, a novel drug, alone and in combination with darolutamide (a hormone therapy) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting patients to find safe doses and evaluate early anti-tumor activity.

items.title: Adding Docetaxel for Metastatic Prostate Cancer with Suboptimal Hormone Therapy Response
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial studies whether adding docetaxel chemotherapy to standard hormone treatment (ADT plus ARPI) improves outcomes in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer patients whose PSA doesn't drop enough with hormone therapy alone. The study is recruiting and tests early chemotherapy intensification.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide vs Enzalutamide Alone in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares the investigational drug mevrometostat combined with enzalutamide against enzalutamide alone in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer patients who haven't received prior hormone therapy or chemotherapy. The study is recruiting to determine if the combination works better than standard treatment.

items.title: FAPI PET/MRI Imaging to Evaluate Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial uses a new imaging technique (FAPI PET/MRI) to better visualize prostate cancer by targeting specific cells in tumor tissue. Patients undergo two research scans to help determine if this approach can improve cancer diagnosis and monitoring compared to standard imaging.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Safety Study in Japanese Patients with Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial evaluates the safety, tolerability, and how the body processes luxdegalutamide (JSB462) in Japanese patients with metastatic prostate cancer. The study is recruiting to establish appropriate dosing in this specific population.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Plus Lutetium-177-PSMA in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial compares two doses of luxdegalutamide (a hormone therapy) combined with lutetium-177-PSMA radioligand therapy against radioligand therapy alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study, no longer recruiting, aims to find the best combination dose for future Phase 3 trials.

items.title: Lutetium-177-PSMA vs Observation for Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer After Definitive Therapy
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial evaluates whether lutetium-177-PSMA radioligand therapy can prevent early-stage oligometastatic prostate cancer from progressing after initial treatment, compared to observation only. The study is recruiting patients to determine if early intervention with this targeted radiation can delay the need for hormone therapy.

items.title: Bipolar Androgen Therapy to Restore Hormone Sensitivity in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial tests whether cycling testosterone levels between very low and very high can make castration-resistant prostate cancer sensitive to hormone therapy again. The study uses testosterone treatment to potentially suppress cancer growth and reduce PSA levels in metastatic disease.

items.title: Actinium-225-PSMA Plus Hormone Therapy vs Standard Care in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares actinium-225-PSMA (alpha-particle radioligand therapy) combined with hormone therapy against standard treatments in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who progressed on one prior hormone therapy. The study is recruiting to determine if this combination improves progression-free survival.

items.title: Inflammation Pathways Drive Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Through Epigenetic Changes
items.summary: This research review describes how chronic inflammation, particularly through NFκB and IL6/JAK/STAT3 pathways, drives prostate cancer progression and treatment resistance. These inflammatory signals work together with androgen receptor signaling to permanently alter how genes are expressed, promoting tumor survival, growth, spread, and resistance to therapy.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances Response to Immunotherapy in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study demonstrates that a next-generation DNA vaccine targeting PSMA can prime the immune system and improve response to PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy. The vaccine prevented tumor growth and lung metastases in animal models and increased anti-tumor immune activity when combined with immunotherapy.

items.title: Ferroptosis as Therapeutic Target in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This review summarizes how ferroptosis (an iron-dependent form of cell death) can be triggered in prostate cancer to overcome drug resistance. Combining ferroptosis-inducing drugs with hormone therapy, chemotherapy, or immunotherapy shows promise in early studies, with several clinical trials underway testing this approach.

items.title: IL-12-Enhanced PSMA CAR T Cell Therapy for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research develops an improved CAR T cell therapy targeting PSMA with added IL-12 to enhance effectiveness. The human-derived cells showed improved specificity, expansion, and anti-tumor activity in laboratory models, addressing safety concerns seen with earlier CAR T approaches.

items.title: Cell-Free DNA for Treatment Selection in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This review discusses how analyzing tumor DNA circulating in the blood (cell-free DNA) can help select treatments for prostate cancer. This non-invasive blood test can detect genetic mutations and monitor treatment response without requiring biopsies.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes Resistance in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research developed a new drug that simultaneously blocks BRD4 and AKT proteins to overcome resistance to AKT inhibitors. The study found that AKT inhibitor resistance is often driven by c-MYC, and blocking both pathways prevents this resistance mechanism in laboratory models of advanced prostate cancer.

items.title: Alternative Theranostic Targets Beyond PSMA in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This review explores emerging targets for imaging and radioligand therapy beyond PSMA, including GRPR, fibroblast activation protein, and others. These alternative targets may help treat prostate cancers with low PSMA expression or provide complementary approaches to expand treatment options.

items.title: Prostatic Acid Phosphatase as Novel Theranostic Target in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This review highlights prostatic acid phosphatase (ACP3) as a promising alternative to PSMA for imaging and radioligand therapy. ACP3 is expressed in over 95% of prostate cancers with minimal expression in normal tissues, potentially offering advantages over PSMA including fewer side effects from off-target uptake.

items.title: Machine Learning Model Predicts Survival in Prostate Cancer with Bone Metastases
items.source: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
items.summary: This study developed a machine learning model to predict survival in non-surgical prostate cancer patients with bone metastases. The analysis found that Gleason score is more important than tumor stage for predicting outcomes, suggesting aggressive treatment should be prioritized for high-grade disease.

items.title: Meta-Analysis of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This comprehensive analysis of 21 trials involving 1,580 patients found that immune checkpoint inhibitors showed modest benefits in unselected metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Combination therapy with checkpoint inhibitors showed better outcomes than single-agent immunotherapy, though results varied across different treatment combinations.
